SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - NOVEMBER 4, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments will be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.

Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. 7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Troop 394.

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Vo, excuse Council/Agency Member
  Bruce W. Barrows from the Monday, November 4, 2024, 7:00 p.m. City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Barrows

  None.

  given by Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action on this item.

 5C.  Review and consideration of selection of a voting delegate and alternate to represent

  Saturday, November 16, 2024 (COUNCIL).

7C.  Award of Contract for Gridley Park East Playground Refurbishment, Project No. 24105,
  Bid No. 1554-24* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Adopt findings in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act, Public
  Resources Code Section 21000 et seq. (CEQA) that the improvements planned under
  the proposed contract award are categorically exempt pursuant to Section 15301 of
  the CEQA Guidelines, based on the findings as set forth in the subject report;

  2. Award a contract to R.E. Schultz Construction, Inc. in the amount of $254,850.00 for
  Gridley Park East Playground Refurbishment project, Capital Project 24105, Bid No.
  1554-24, and reject the other bids; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or designee to execute any project-related change
  orders, in accordance with the City’s adopted Purchasing and Contracting Policy
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 – 1 - 0) as follows:

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration for the Cerritos City Council to identify the priority goals to
  guide the preparation of the City’s Fiscal Year 2025-26 Budget and Strategic Financial
  Plan in accordance with the Strategic Financial Plan and Budget Preparation Policy
  (Policy 2.04) (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Drew Schneider, Director of Administrative Services, and
  Mike Egan, Christine Martin, and Kylie Sun, representatives from the City’s Strategic
  Plan consulting firm, Tripepi Smith. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting the
  Council/Agency members received full-text, unredacted copies of the three (3) written
  comment(s) submitted for Item 9A by the deadline listed on the agenda and for
  inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted
  for this meeting can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk.

  Sam Desai provided suggestions for City strategic planning goal priorities.

  Bin Tang spoke regarding low resident engagement in the City strategic plan
  community survey and inquired as to how the City may attain higher levels of
  community engagement.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding low resident engagement in the City strategic plan
  community survey and inquired as to how the City may attain higher levels of
  community engagement.

  Adriana T. spoke regarding low resident engagement in the City strategic plan
  community survey and inquired as to how the City may attain higher levels of
  community engagement. She also expressed gratitude for the City’s response to her
  suggestions she provided in response at the City Strategic Planning Community
  Workshop.

  Patricia Bautista expressed gratitude for the City’s response to her suggestions she
  provided in response at the City Strategic Planning Community Workshop.

  Adrian Ayub provided suggestions for City strategic planning goal priorities.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Approve the eight (8) strategic planning goals presented for discussion, as follows:

  a.  Enhance Public Safety;
  b.  Assess and Maintain Infrastructure;
  c.  Strengthen Economic Development;
  d.  Improve Technology Resources;
  e.  Attract and Retain a Highly-Skilled Workforce;
  f.  Focus on Fiscal Transparency and Sustainability;
  g.  Improve Community Communications; and
  h.  Ensure Continued Excellence in Community Recreation and Cultural
  Programming; and

  2. Direct the City Manager or designee to work in collaboration with Tripepi Smith and
  the Budget and Finance Ad Hoc Working Group to develop measureable objectives
  and tasks for achieving the City Council’s priority goals, and identify to which
  departments the goals apply, for presentation to the City Council for review and
  final consideration at a future date and time (COUNCIL).

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT:

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, provided the following Closed Session report:

  The City Council convened into Closed Session to discuss Items 12A, 12B, 12C, 12D, and
  12E.

  Items 12A, 12B, and 12C:
  The City Council received a briefing on Items 12A, 12B, and 12C, and no reportable action
  was taken. There was nothing further to report.

  Item 12D:
  Item 12D was not considered.

  Item 12E:
  The City Council completed its performance evaluation for the City Attorney and reported
  that the City Council has chosen to transition the appointment of the City Attorney to the
  City’s prior Acting City Attorney, Pam Lee, and transition the City Attorney’s Office to the
  law firm of Aleshire and Wynder, LLP. The City Council reported that they will honor the
  minimum thirty (30)-day notice provisions for terminating the current Agreement for
  Contract Legal Services and directed the current City Attorney and City Manager to
  coordinate and take appropriate actions to transition the City Attorney’s contract for services
  to Pam Lee and Aleshire and Wynder, LLP, and to retain Bill Ihrke and Rutan and Tucker,
  LLP as Special Counsel to complete specific tasks and projects. There was nothing further to
  report.
